topology: PC1 → R1 (OSPF10) → R2 (OSPF10/EIGRP100 boundary) → R3 (EIGRP100) → SRV1. R3 also advertises a diagnostic Loopback0 /32 into EIGRP. Addresses, passive LAN membership, exact source prefix lists and tagging maps are prepared. Initial faults select static instead of EIGRP for the OSPF export and omit the EIGRP seed metric for the OSPF return export.
implemented: Fifth ENARSI Layer3 lab with independent practice/completed variants, five-row addressing/role plan, staged troubleshooting guide, working reference, accessible section counts and current-site domain/path/query permalinks. Existing ENARSI labs,39 ENCOR entries and other categories remain available.

Initial diagnosis correlates three real client No route drops at R1 with healthy OSPF/EIGRP adjacencies and installed source routes on R2. Repairing only EIGRP-to-OSPF export produces a received service Type5 LSA and O E2 route tagged100, but no EIGRP return route. Three requests reach SRV1 and their parent-linked echo replies are dropped at R3, proving one-way forwarding rather than treating a timeout as sufficient evidence.

The exact EIGRP default metric100000/100/255/1/1500 restores received D EX client reachability on R3: AD170, metric53760, tag200, next hop10.0.23.1. Forward O E2 remains AD110, metric20, tag100 via10.0.12.2. Actual destination acceptance, router sends and parent-linked replies prove three successful pings in each direction.

Export scope compares successful R2-originated diagnostic pings against three real R1 No route drops for PC1, with no diagnostic external LSA on R1. Exact prefix-list/route-map permits exclude unrelated source routes through implicit deny while tagging only the intended service and client exports.

Controlled seed removal and client-prefix denial independently withdraw the EIGRP return route while preserving the OSPF service route. Each incident requires three actual request-delivery/reply-drop failures and fresh three-reply proofs in both directions after repair.

A service interface shutdown on R3 withdraws its connected source, R2 learned EIGRP route and remote R1 external advertisement. Three actual No route drops precede restoration and new service replies. Server power loss or interface toggles without observed failure cannot impersonate the prescribed incident.

A working E1 stage receives external seed20 and installs metric21 after internal OSPF cost1; actual service replies are required before restoration to E2 metric20 and new replies. HTTP completion requires the complete real200 response with the expected page, matching server transaction and routed request.

Fourteen tasks combine five live policy/state/save goals with nine observations. Practice starts0/14; the completed reference supplies5/14 without fabricated traffic. Per-attempt epochs and normal simulator notifications capture synchronous CLI evidence with a closed guide. Earned observations survive portable export/import; live state and startup equality revoke on drift.

Native negative-delivery tests block R2 OSPF advertisements or reliable EIGRP UPDATE datagrams and prove remote external routes cannot appear before delivery. Broad policies, wrong tags, static shortcuts, altered memberships, broken gateways and unsaved changes fail the appropriate live goals.

No simulation engine, network protocol implementation, global UI, terminal styling or node artwork changed. The exercise uses existing packet-driven OSPF/EIGRP, route maps, seed metrics, route withdrawal, ping, traceroute and HTTP.
scope: IOS IPv4 troubleshooting at a single OSPF/EIGRP redistribution boundary. This new lab has native and browser validation, not a fresh CML capture. It does not claim multiple-ASBR feedback prevention, arbitrary process-ID fault fidelity, IPv6 redistribution or NX-OS.
